GATE: PASS (hard limit p99 <= 200 ms held; final p99 199.0 ms)
Final settings (config.json): batch_size 4, workers 14, prefetch 0
Final throughput: 700.0 req/s, p99 199.0 ms (bench.py: "within the 200 ms limit")
Before: batch_size 8, workers 1, prefetch 0 -> 100.0 req/s, p99 197.2 ms

Method
- The SPEC wall: p99 never above 200 ms. Treated as a wall, not a score. Every candidate config was checked against it and any config over 200 ms was refused outright, never traded for throughput.
- bench.py is deterministic (same config, same numbers). I evaluated bench.measure over the full feasible grid: batch_size 1..19, workers 1..39, prefetch 0..39. That covers every config that can stay under 200 ms (batch >= 9 alone gives p99 >= 215.6 ms; workers > 26 or prefetch > 36 alone exceed 200 ms). 1174 configs pass the wall.
- Best within the wall: 700.0 req/s at batch 4, workers 14, prefetch 0 (p99 199.0 ms). Next best: 687.5 req/s at batch 5, workers 11 (p99 200.0 ms, exactly on the limit).
- Ran bench.py twice on the final config.json: same numbers both times.

Not done / open
- n = 1 distinct measurement per config; the bench is a deterministic model, so repeats give identical numbers. Real-service variance is not measured here.
- The margin to the wall is 1.0 ms. If the real service has run-to-run noise, a safer choice is batch 4, workers 13, prefetch 0: 650.0 req/s at p99 193.2 ms. Owner's call.
- No gate.py or gate.json exists in the work folder, so no build/test/scan/mutation gate was run; the check above is the SPEC wall via bench.py.
